newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng scores record closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng scores record closing high.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index ended at a record closing high on Friday, as investors cheered an overnight fall in the U.S. long bond yield following the release of friendly U.S. economic data, traders said.
The Hang Seng index closed 51.71 points higher at a record close of 12,529.27. The previous record close was 12,510.05 reached on October 18.

"Look at the long bond. It really was something," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities. "There is a very strong correlation between the Hang Seng index and the (long bond) yield," he said.

The U.S. long bond surged 25/32 on Thursday, pushing the yield down to 6.64 percent after the release of U.S. weekly jobless claims and Chicago purchasing managers data. The data suggested the inflation outlook remains tame.
"Overall we are still optimistic the market is poised to challenge the recent intra-day record high," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
The Hang Seng index hit an intra-day record high of 12,602.34 points on October 16.
"Wall Street is not going to have a sharp correction because of the latest economic data so that is why the U.S. long bond yield is still trapped well below 6.8 percent now," said Tang.
Friday's market turnover was HK$7.30 billion, up from HK$6.34 billion on Thursday.

The blue chip index hit a session high of 12,562.12 on Friday but traders said it eased off that level due to some caution about U.S. October jobs data due later on Friday and next week's U.S. presidential election.

"If it wasn't for the uncertainty happening in the States tonight and next week with the election then the index would probably be able to make some further gains," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
HSBC was the biggest net gainer, rising HK$2.00 to close at HK$159.50 after hitting a new record high of HK$160.00 during the session. Hang Seng Bank rose HK$0.75 to HK$92.50.
New World Development jumped HK$1.00 to HK$46.00 and Henderson Land advanced HK$1.25 to HK$70.00.
HongKong Telecom fell HK$0.10 to HK$13.55. The company is due to release interim results on Tuesday.
